result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would erase the concept of *scarcity*—not just of resources, but of empathy, time, and possibility. Imagine a world where no one hoards, no one fears lack, and no one justifies cruelty because they believe there isn’t "enough." No more wars over land, no more children hungry while food rots, no more art or love or ideas suppressed because someone decided they were "too much" for others to share.

The ripple effects would be vast: greed would collapse without its fuel, generosity would be the default, and every person could spend their life *creating* instead of competing. Even conflict would transform—debates could be about vision, not survival.

(But then again… maybe the tension of scarcity is what forces us to invent, to fight, to *care* so fiercely. So perhaps the real change would be to keep scarcity’s lessons—urgency, gratitude, resilience—while stripping away its suffering. A paradox, I know. Humans are full of them.)

What about you? What single thread would you pull to unravel the world as it is?
